summary: The Ninja Forms - File Uploads add-on for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion (and...
description: The Ninja Forms - File Uploads add-on for WordPress is vulnerable to Arbitrary File Deletion (and arbitrary file read via S3/Dropbox/Google Drive exfiltration) in versions up to, and including, 3.3.36. The flaw spans NF_FU_Fields_Upload::process() in includes/fields/upload.php — which returns early (leaving the client-supplied files[] intact) whenever a public submission carries a nonempty extra.saveProgress — and NF_FU_External_Abstracts_Service::process_upload() in includes/external/abstracts/service.php, whose authoritative-path reload only fires when the client sends upload_id. By omitting upload_id, an attacker's data[file_path] survives into the Background Upload queue and is used by both upload_file_to_s3() (as SourceFile) and the maybe_delete_server_file() unlink() call in includes/external/abstracts/backgroundupload.php, with no canonicalization or upload-directory containment check (the plugin's own is_path_within_upload_dir() helper is only applied on admin paths). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to delete arbitrary files on the affected site's server which may make remote code execution possible — specifically, deleting wp-config.php forces WordPress into its setup screen, enabling full site takeover.

summary: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in Apache Roller. When Roller sends a weblog...

This issue affects Apache Roller from 4.0 through 6.1.6. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 6.1.7, which removes the unsafe deserialization.

The request-token check applied only to POST requests, and administrative actions also accepted GET requests. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which requires POST and a valid token for actions that change data.

The entry was removed from the weblog but stayed in the search index, and public search showed its content. AtomPub is disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which shows only published entries in search results.

summary: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6...
description: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows any logged-in user to learn other users' email addresses. The user search in the authoring interface shows only user names, but it also matched the search text against email addresses, so a user could confirm an address one character at a time. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which matches only user names for users who are not administrators.

summary: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6...
description: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows a weblog administrator to read another user's stored password hash by authoring a custom weblog template that reaches the wrapped persistent object behind the template's weblog or entry data, rather than the reduced set of fields the wrapper is meant to expose. Roller treats weblog administrators as untrusted and exposes weblog and entry data to templates only through wrapper classes, but a public accessor on those wrapper classes returned the underlying persistent object directly, including the stored password hash of the weblog's creator and of any author whose entry renders on the page. No non-default configuration is required; this affects any weblog whose administrator can author templates. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which removes template access to the underlying wrapped objects.

cwes.name: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

summary: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows...
description: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with no weblog permissions to read files readable by the Roller process and cause the server to issue outbound HTTP requests to attacker-chosen destinations, by submitting a crafted Atom entry to the AtomPub endpoint. The entry body is parsed with a parser configuration that permits external parameter entities and external DTD subsets, and the parse happens before any per-weblog authorization check and before any check of whether the AtomPub feature is enabled, so the endpoint is reachable by any authenticated account on a default installation. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which parses AtomPub entries with a hardened XML configuration and rejects AtomPub requests while the feature is disabled.

summary: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache...
description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with the Author role on a weblog that uses a custom theme to store script that runs in the browser of anyone who opens the file's resource URL. The fix for CVE-2026-82387 serves uploaded media as a download unless it is an image, audio, video, PDF or plain text, but media files found through a custom theme were served with the type their path implies, and the upload form let the uploader choose that path. Media uploads are disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which serves these files under the same rules as other media and no longer accepts the path from the upload form.

summary: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in the Planet feed aggregator administration of Apache Roller 4...
description: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) in the Planet feed aggregator administration of Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated attacker to make the Roller server fetch a URL the attacker chooses, including internal addresses, by inducing a logged-in global administrator to open a crafted web page. The action that adds a Planet subscription can be triggered cross-site; in recent releases it accepts GET requests, which Roller's CSRF token check does not cover. The action fetches the supplied URL and saves the subscription, and any fetched content that parses as a feed is then published without authentication in the aggregated Planet feed. The Planet aggregator is enabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which requires POST requests with a valid CSRF token for Planet administration changes and turns the Planet aggregator off by default.

summary: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache...
description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') in Apache Roller 5.0.1 through 6.1.6 allows an authenticated user with the Author role on a weblog to store script in entry tags submitted through AtomPub. Roller's tag filter allowed HTML characters in tag names, and the bundled gaurav, fauxcoly and frontpage themes and the showEntryTags macro print tag names without escaping, so the script runs in the browser of anyone who views the weblog. This matters when weblog authors are not trusted with script (weblogAdminsUntrusted=true, the default since 6.1.4). AtomPub is disabled by default. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which removes HTML characters from tag names, including names stored earlier.

summary: Missing Authorization in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows any logged-in user to read...
description: Missing Authorization in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows any logged-in user to read unpublished entries of a weblog they have no role in. The entry preview checked that the user was logged in, but not that the user had a role in the weblog being previewed. The attacker must know the weblog name and the entry's link name. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later, which requires a role in the weblog to preview its entries.

summary: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6...
description: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor in Apache Roller 4.0 through 6.1.6 allows an unauthenticated visitor to recover the email addresses of people who left approved comments. The search index stored commenter email addresses, and the public weblog search accepted queries on that field, including wildcard queries that confirm an address one character at a time. Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.7 or later and rebuild the search index.

summary: A flaw was found in the login-failure storage component of Keycloak, the identity and access...
description: A flaw was found in the login-failure storage component of Keycloak, the identity and access management solution. This issue specifically affects deployments using MySQL or MariaDB databases in a multi-node configuration. When multiple failed login attempts occur simultaneously for the same account, a synchronization error can cause the system to enter a repetitive loop that locks the user's record in the database. This results in legitimate login attempts for that user being blocked and failing with an error. Furthermore, because some failures are not correctly recorded during this loop, the system's brute-force protection may not accurately count all failed attempts.
